national_raw_news.title: India records $11.3 bn FPIs in first 18 days of November: CEA Anantha Nageswaran
national_raw_news.content: Chief Economic Adviser, Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran today said that foreign capital is returning sharply to India as oil prices cool below 100 dollars per barrel and the emerging risks regarding AI valuation. Addressing the 65th General Assembly and Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE) in Mumbai, Dr. Nageswaran said India has recorded foreign portfolio inflows of 11.3 billion dollars in just the first 18 days of November. The CEA further underlined that India remains poised to be a big beneficiary in the course of the next financial year as the AI bubble comes down to realistic levels, adding that earlier currency pressures from AI outflows will now likely turn into a source of currency strength. He also highlighted that India has sustained roughly 7 per cent real GDP growth despite global tariff turmoil, supply shocks, and geopolitical conflicts, adding that India has been successful in lifting roughly 500 million people above the 4.20 dollar-a-day moderate poverty line, with rural poverty falling faster than urban in the past decade. While noting that the Indian Government, which had been cautious about trade liberalisation until around 2020, Dr. Nageswaran said that the government has embraced free trade agreements with considerable enthusiasm in the post-pandemic period. He said that India has not only concluded but also operationalised trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand this year alone. He added that a trade agreement with the European Union has also been concluded while trade agreements with the US and Canada are also imminent. Pointing towards India’s strong export performance in the current financial year, the CEA said exports of goods and services stood at around 569 billion dollars from April to October, registering a growth of nearly 17 percent. Talking about the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the CEA flagged five unique challenges – geopolitical fragmentation, China’s manufacturing scale, the energy trilemma, AI-led job shifts, and social media’s impact on youth cognitive skills. To counter these, the CEA said closing technology gaps will buy resilience for India, while agriculture, trade skills, and human-centric services will buy leverage for India.

Top Stories of the Day Share DD India November 20, 2026 8:22 AM IST Prime Minister | SCO | Shanghai Cooperation Organisation | SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum | Narendra Modi | PM Modi PM Modi to inaugurate first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi on November 20 Author: DD India Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi on November 20, at around 5:30 PM. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The three-day Forum, scheduled from November 20 to 22, aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of SCO member countries, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation. The initiative follows a proposal made by PM Modi at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025 to establish a dedicated platform for civilisational dialogue under the SCO framework. The proposal was subsequently welcomed in the Bishkek Declaration of the organisation. Cultural showcase to highlight India-Eurasia connections The inaugural ceremony will feature a cultural presentation titled “Civilisations in Conversation – Cultural Show”, combining music, dance, visual storytelling and narration. Based on the theme “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – The World Is One Family”, the presentation will highlight cultural connections between India and the wider Eurasian region. The Forum will also host exhibitions showcasing India’s archaeological, artistic and literary heritage under the title “ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence.” The exhibition will offer visitors an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE. It will include excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries. Another key attraction will be the “Mahabharat Scroll Pavilion – Anant: A Rare 18th Century Mahabharata Scroll”, featuring an illustrated scroll that reflects India’s rich epic and artistic traditions. Four thematic sessions to explore shared civilisational heritage Four thematic sessions will be organised on November 21 and 22, bringing together scholars, academics, subject experts and cultural representatives from across the SCO region. The discussions will explore a range of shared cultural and intellectual traditions, including music and performing arts, textiles, cuisine and traditional games. Participants will also examine common traditions in art and architecture, as well as language and literary heritage, including scripts and manuscripts. Monastic trails and philosophical traditions will form another key area of discussion. national_raw_news.title: Srinagar to get Rs 361 cr waste processing facility at Achan - Rising Kashmir
national_raw_news.content: Srinagar to get Rs 361 cr waste processing facility at Achan Advertisment Breaking News Top Stories Srinagar to get Rs 361 cr waste processing facility at Achan RK News 20 Nov 2026 03:32 IST Follow Us 125-tonne construction waste plant targeted for Dec 91,789 tonnes of accumulated material processed at dumpsite Srinagar, Nov 19: In a major move to strengthen solid waste management in Srinagar, the Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC) has proposed an integrated waste processing facility with a capacity of 800 tonnes per day at Achan, involving an estimated investment of Rs 361 crore, while 91,789 tonnes of accumulated waste have already been processed at the dumpsite as part of efforts to reclaim the site and reduce environmental risks. Joint Commissioner, Srinagar Municipal Corporation, Syed Abul Qasim, disclosed these details during a press briefing organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, in collaboration with the Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee (JKPCC) on Thursday to discuss the implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. Qasim said the proposed facility at Achan would include multiple waste processing components aimed at reducing dependence on conventional dumping and improving the recovery of reusable materials. The project, estimated to cost Rs 361 crore, will have facilities for material recovery, compressed biogas generation, composting and refuse-derived fuel processing. He said the integrated facility would enable the processing of different categories of municipal waste and support efforts to recover useful resources from waste generated across Srinagar. Highlighting the ongoing work at the Achan dumpsite near Anchar Lake, Qasim said approximately 91,789 tonnes of waste had already been processed as part of measures to reclaim the site and address environmental concerns associated with accumulated waste. The processing work, he said, is aimed at recovering useful materials, reducing the volume of accumulated waste and limiting environmental risks at the site. The Joint Commissioner also informed that a leachate treatment plant has been proposed at Achan to address environmental concerns arising from liquid waste generated at the dumping site. Leachate, the contaminated liquid that forms when water passes through accumulated waste, requires treatment to prevent potential pollution of surrounding soil and water resources. In another development, Qasim said a construction and demolition waste processing plant with a capacity of 125 tonnes per day is projected to be completed by December 2026. The facility is intended to strengthen the city's capacity to process waste generated from construction and demolition activities rather than allowing such material to accumulate at dumping locations. The proposed projects form part of SMC's efforts to improve waste processing infrastructure and address longstanding waste management challenges in the city. Meanwhile, Chairman JKPCC, Vasu Yadav, said the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, introduce stricter provisions for waste segregation, scientific processing and accountability among waste generators. He said the new framework requires segregation of waste at source into four categories — wet waste, dry waste, sanitary waste and special care waste. The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, in collaboration with JKPCC, organised a press briefing to explain the key provisions of the new Rules and sensitise media organisations and the public about the responsibilities of different stakeholders. The Rules place particular emphasis on segregation of waste at source into four categories—wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste. The framework also seeks to strengthen scientific waste processing, recycling, resource recovery and remediation of legacy dumpsites, while ensuring greater accountability among waste generators. JKPCC Chairman Vasu Yadav said the Rules provide for measures such as user fees, spot fines and environmental compensation to ensure compliance. He stressed that effective implementation would require coordinated action by government agencies, institutions, commercial establishments and citizens. Yadav said source segregation and scientific processing must become an integral part of waste management practices, adding that recycling and resource recovery were important for reducing the burden on disposal sites. In her opening remarks, Director PIB Jammu Neha Jalali said the press briefing was organised to familiarise media organisations and the public with the provisions of the Rules and promote awareness about responsible waste disposal. She said effective implementation would require behavioural change and active participation of citizens, institutions and local authorities. Jalali also highlighted the role of the media in disseminating information, encouraging source segregation and taking the message of cleanliness and sustainable waste management to the grassroots to achieve the objectives of Swachh Bharat. Commissioner Jammu Municipal Corporation Ayushi Sudan highlighted the Corporation’s initiatives to strengthen waste management and improve accountability among bulk waste generators.
